experiments.title: First OpenCouncil benchmark run of the fine-tune
experiments.question: Does the LoRA fine-tune beat commercial ASR on the OpenCouncil benchmark?
experiments.conclusion: On the held-out slice the fine-tune tied commercial providers (0.151 vs 0.147-0.154). The apparent win over base whisper was a cross-stack artifact.
experiments.decision: Do not cite these numbers as model quality. The adapter used carried the label-prefix bug.

experiments.title: Label-prefix bug in the training targets
experiments.question: Were training targets shifted one position on every sample?
experiments.conclusion: Yes. Every run before 2026-08-01 trained on shifted labels.
experiments.decision: All pre-2026-08-01 adapters are KNOWN_BROKEN. Retrain before citing any of them.

experiments.title: Base vs fine-tune through one decoder stack
experiments.question: Is the fine-tune's +1.54 deletion gap a property of the weights or of the decoder?
experiments.conclusion: Of the decoder. On a neutral stack the gap collapses to +0.19 with a CI containing zero. The only effect surviving is substitutions, -0.61 [-0.81, -0.40].
experiments.decision: Never compare two models across two stacks. The continuous-30s-window proposal lost its empirical motivation.
caveats: The fine-tune arm used artifact-adapter-july-broken, NOT the corrected adapter. Established 2026-08-10 by re-decoding 3 windows and byte-comparing: 3/3 match the broken adapter, 0/3 match the corrected one. The report did not name its artifact.

experiments.title: Mixture ratio 20/80 vs 50/50
experiments.question: Does a 20/80 corrections-to-backbone mixture beat 50/50?
experiments.conclusion: Inconclusive by the frozen rule. C - A = -0.24 points, 90% [-0.89, +0.36]. Per-seed spread is 2.1 points, ten times the effect.
experiments.decision: Closed by user instruction 2026-08-09: do not reopen. Seed variance dominates at this sample size.

experiments.title: Packed 30s clips, with and without timestamp supervision
experiments.question: Does training on packed ~30s clips help, and does timestamp supervision help on top?
experiments.conclusion: Neither arm beat the corrected single-utterance adapter on 32 dev windows. P - Pn = +1.54 points but the CI contains zero and the per-window sign is not consistent (11 worse / 10 better / 11 tied).
experiments.decision: STOP: do not buy a second seed for timestamp supervision. The packing infrastructure is built and verified if ever needed again.
caveats: Codex audit 2026-08-10: arithmetic reproduces exactly from raw per-clip counts, but four claims in the original prose overran the evidence and were corrected. The timestamp mechanism is a hypothesis, not a finding.
The base - A gap of 5.58 points draws 67% of its 69 errors from ONE window (rclip_024). Without it the gap is 1.95 points.

experiments.title: The corrected adapter on the OpenCouncil benchmark
experiments.question: Does the corrected (post-label-prefix-fix) adapter beat base whisper and the commercial providers on the 260-window benchmark?
experiments.conclusion: On the 40 training-disjoint windows (argos+orestiada, 12,194 words) the corrected adapter scores 0.1548 wer-nofillers: statistically indistinguishable from Scribe v2 (+1.14, 90% [-0.58, +2.79]) and Soniox (+1.26, [-0.33, +2.80]), and better than base whisper (-2.30, [-4.02, -0.77]) and than its own broken predecessor (-1.77, [-2.66, -0.98]). 260/260 items, 0 errors, $0.30.
experiments.decision: The label-prefix fix bought a real 1.77 points on unseen cities, sign consistent (26 windows better / 11 worse / 3 tied). Publish the corrected adapter. Do not read the base comparison as a weights effect - it is cross-stack.
caveats: 7 of the 260 windows are meetings dated >= 2026-06-01, inside the temporal TEST definition; one of them (win_argos_jun3_2026_855222) supplied 21% of the base comparison. Re-measured on the 39 clean validation windows every conclusion survives: ours 0.1542, vs base -1.87 [-3.35,-0.50], vs broken -1.58 [-2.41,-0.85], vs Scribe +1.12 [-0.54,+2.73], vs Soniox +1.19 [-0.48,+2.70]. Exclude those 7 from any future final measurement.
argos+orestiada is part of the VALIDATION set, not the test set, and has been scored repeatedly and used to decide which experiments to stop. Treat the number as potentially optimistically biased.
The base-whisper arm runs on the HuggingFace serverless pipeline, a different decoder stack. The -2.30 includes an engine difference.
The broken-adapter arm ran on an RTX 3090 in July, ours on an RTX A4000 today. Measured separately: CPU int8 and CUDA int8 give different tokens from the same artifact, so the device is not neutral.
The reference is OpenCouncil's own published text, so this measures agreement-with-OpenCouncil, not accuracy.
One seed. The mixture experiment measured 2.1 points of per-seed spread, larger than the 1.77 claimed here.

experiments.title: Full LoRA training run
experiments.question: Does the full training recipe produce a usable adapter?
experiments.conclusion: Reported gains were measured against unfairly-served baselines, and the run carried the label-prefix bug.
experiments.decision: Do not migrate or cite. Retrained as exp-2026-08-02-fulltrain-corrected.

experiments.title: Contextual biasing with roster hotwords
experiments.question: Can inference-time biasing get the name accuracy the fine-tune was supposed to buy?
experiments.conclusion: Measured properly on the corrected adapter (artifact-ct2-fixed, 39 frozen validation windows, CPU int8, preregistered hash-ordered 160-token surname hotwords, meeting-clustered bootstrap): biasing does lift names - mention recall 51.2%->65.4%, precision 93.3%->96.4%, substitutions -82 with CI excluding zero - but it CAUSES deletions: +133 (del_rate +0.0112 [+0.0020,+0.0207], CI excludes zero). Net WER +0.34 points [-0.61,+1.31]; fails the preregistered non-inferiority gate (upper bound +0.0131 vs margin +0.0010). The mechanism is prompt-induced skipping: hotwords share the 448-token decoder context. The 2026-07-25 name-subset signal is confirmed directionally, but the WER cost lands on the deletion side, our worst error class.
experiments.decision: Do not ship decode-time hotword biasing. The post-hoc roster repair arm of exp-2026-08-11-name-repair delivers name correction (-30 subs, -0.25 WER, CI excludes zero, zero collateral) with no decode cost and no deletion penalty; name work continues there. The preregistered exploratory 200-token secondary was NOT run: the failure mechanism (longer prompt -> more skipping) predicts it is worse, and the primary already failed its gate.
caveats: Stack: CPU int8, beam=5, faster-whisper `hotwords` param (not initial_prompt). The mini-PC serves beam=2 on GPU; magnitudes do not transfer unchecked, but the deletion mechanism is decoder-context arithmetic and should.
160-token budget holds ~20 of 32-36 roster surnames per meeting (hash-decorrelated exclusions); full coverage is impossible under faster-whisper's 223-token hotword cap.
Raw results: ~/.cache/oc-public/serving-stack/results-B-eval.json (eval-B-hotwords.json hypotheses). Harness scripts/serving_stack/hotwords_arm.py, 26 tests.

experiments.title: Where the fine-tune's gain comes from
experiments.question: Which part of the training signal produces the measured gain?
experiments.conclusion: The gain decomposes into edit-bias from corrections rather than general acoustic adaptation.
experiments.decision: Treat the correction dataset as a lexical signal, not an acoustic one.

experiments.title: The 'lexical costume' thesis
experiments.question: Is the correction dataset a lexical signal wearing an acoustic costume?
experiments.conclusion: Supported. The LLM post-editor reached 0.155 -> 0.119 WER on 50 corrected utterances, better than fine-tuning.
experiments.decision: Pursue post-editing and biasing over further acoustic fine-tuning.

experiments.title: A gate for the LLM post-editor
experiments.question: Can the post-editor be made safe enough to ship?
experiments.conclusion: Yes, with a gate. The gate is what makes it work; ungated it occasionally rewrites correct text.
experiments.decision: Any post-editor ships with its gate.

experiments.title: Full run with the corrected objective
experiments.question: Does fixing the label prefix change the outcome?
experiments.conclusion: Same data, same recipe, correct labels. This produced artifact-adapter-fixed.

experiments.title: Why the fine-tune loses to base
experiments.question: Why does the fine-tune underperform base whisper?
experiments.conclusion: 48% corrections teach an edit bias; the 52% no-edit rows teach imitation.
experiments.decision: Rebalance or rethink the mixture. Followed by exp-2026-08-08-mixture-ratio.

experiments.title: Combining ASR systems
experiments.question: Does combining several ASR systems beat the best single one?
experiments.conclusion: Yes. A free 3-way vote beats the best single system by 1.1 points, and the LLM is not what does it.
experiments.decision: Fusion is a real, cheap win. Not yet productised.

experiments.title: Overlap as an error marker
experiments.question: Does speaker overlap predict transcription error?
experiments.conclusion: Overlap is rare (2.2%) but the top quartile scores ~10 points worse, consistently across all seven systems.
experiments.decision: Worth a causal test, which became exp-2026-08-03-synthetic-overlap.

experiments.title: The causal overlap test
experiments.question: Does adding a real interjector actually cost accuracy?
experiments.conclusion: Adding a real interjector costs 0.16 points against a frozen gate of 2.0.
experiments.decision: Overlap-handling (DiCoW) closed. Not worth building.

experiments.title: Cutting at speaker changes
experiments.question: Does segmenting at speaker changes help?
experiments.conclusion: Worth nothing measurable. The control arm is what made the number readable.
experiments.decision: Closed. Keep the control-arm habit.

experiments.title: What the benchmark reference actually is
experiments.question: Is the benchmark reference independent of our pipeline?
experiments.conclusion: No. Benchmark reference vs our published transcript: WER 0.0008. It is our own output.
experiments.decision: The benchmark measures agreement-with-OpenCouncil, not accuracy. It records, it does not decide.

experiments.question: Were words two systems catch but the reference lacks actually spoken?
experiments.conclusion: 70.5% of them were really spoken.
experiments.decision: The published reference under-transcribes. Build an audio-faithful reference.

experiments.question: How much unseen council audio is reachable?
experiments.conclusion: The public API yields 151 untouched meetings with speaker rosters, ~200 hours.
experiments.decision: This is the pool for any future evaluation cohort.

experiments.question: How far is the published text from what a careful listener hears?
experiments.conclusion: 17.5% disagreement with audio on unseen meetings.
experiments.decision: Fidelity-to-audio becomes the deciding metric.

experiments.conclusion: Yes. Tied on the old metric, the fine-tune is +4.9 points on what a human heard.

experiments.title: Consolidated training brief
experiments.question: What has been tried, on what data, with what result - as one document?
experiments.conclusion: Dataset: 22.47h train (11.16h human corrections + 11.32h unverified no_edit labels), 2.79s mean clip, 209 meetings, 9 cities, Aug 2024 - May 2026. Ten adapters trained. Only the label-prefix fix produced a measured gain.
experiments.decision: Use this as the input document when designing the next training run.

experiments.title: Where the gap to Scribe actually is
experiments.question: What kinds of errors separate our adapter from Scribe v2, and which are worth attacking?
experiments.conclusion: The 1.12-point gap is concentrated, not diffuse: the 8 worst windows account for 193 errors while the total gap is 133, so we are ahead in aggregate on the other 31. Four patterns: 2 decoder-degeneration windows, 2 name-dense windows (roll call, agenda), lost short speaker turns, and number/protocol formatting. 21.6% of our substitution errors are person or place names, almost all off by 1-2 characters. Style conventions favour US, not Scribe, so the true acoustic gap is larger than 1.12. Taxonomy pass: our deficit is +3.49 pts in real recognition categories, offset by -2.51 in convention categories (of which -2.27 is number formatting and insertions). Neutralise the convention and the true acoustic gap is ~3.5 points, not 1.0. Deletion-to-insertion ratio 3.3:1 vs Scribe's 1.6:1.
experiments.decision: Do not retrain to close this gap. A per-meeting name lexicon (~0.4-0.6 pts) plus anti-hallucination decoding config (~0.5 pts) attack ~0.9-1.1 of the 1.12 points with no training. Diacritics, generic spell post-editing and reference-style mimicry are dead ends.
caveats: Per-window we lose on 24 and win on 12; the aggregate favours us on the non-worst windows only because our wins are larger. Not 'broadly better with exceptions'.
The a/b/c split (60-65% genuine / 15-20% style / 15-20% bad reference) is a qualitative estimate from 8 windows, not a measurement.

experiments.title: Post-hoc name repair and decoder ablations
experiments.question: Can a roster-based name lexicon and anti-degeneration decoding close the gap without retraining, net positive?
experiments.next_action: The E arm is measured and survives everywhere it can fire (validation -0.25; benchmark look pooled -0.08, unseen -0.28; holdout no-op for lack of rosters). What remains is DEPLOYMENT: wire per-meeting roster + per-city term files (now exist for all 10 benchmark cities, mechanically generated and hash-frozen 2026-08-12) into the serving endpoint in shadow mode, add the v2 alias fix for the two registry-vs-reference orthography conflicts (Αδραχτάς/Καδόλου), and judge the Βήμα-3 gates on untouched meetings. See docs/reports/2026-08-12-serving-stack-ladder.md.
caveats: Codex review: the decoder work is NOT one config - no_speech_threshold deletes speech, temperature fallback generates new garbage, overlap merge duplicates words. Separate ablations, and it does not go first.
The right comparison is paired against our own current system on identical weights, not against Scribe. Seed variance then does not enter.

The decoder-ablation half of this question is ANSWERED by exp-2026-08-12-decode-ablation (2026-08-12) and should not be rerun: no_speech_threshold cannot delete speech here because the gate fires zero times on the 39 validation windows, and removing the temperature fallback makes deletions and insertions worse, not better. What remains open is only the name-lexicon arm, which keeps its own gate in docs/specs/2026-08-11-name-repair-plan.md.

experiments.title: Desk research: what non-training levers remain
experiments.question: Which remaining improvement directions survive sourced external research and an adversarial reconciliation pass?
experiments.conclusion: Four-report arc (Grok live search + Codex second reader + adversarial reconciliation). Standing findings: (a) the dominant residual error class vs Scribe is homophone orthography the audio cannot decide, and scale does not buy it back (closest published analogue: ~1300h for ~0.5 pts); (b) deletions are the fixable half and the serving decode config had never been examined; (c) the correction-only-vs-full dataset ablation is the cheapest unanswered question (one GPU run, zero human hours); (d) the verbatim standard (filled pauses, false starts) is an institutional decision and a prerequisite for compatible future data; (e) no published ASR work on municipal councils exists in any language; vendor accuracy claims are not comparable.
experiments.decision: Executed as docs/specs/2026-08-11-endgame-handoff-plan.md: decode ablation, DS-WER, correction-only ablation, final report. Encoder unfreezing, generic corpora (Common Voice/FLEURS), HParl staging and more raw hours are set aside.
caveats: The first two reports carry same-day corrections; where they disagree, 2026-08-11-review-reconciliation.md is the authoritative reading of the arc.
Rankings inside individual reports mix metrics (name recall vs WER) and evaluation sets; do not sum their expected gains.
Codex timed out on the full research prompt; questions 3, 5 and 6 of the prompt have no second reader.

experiments.title: DS-WER against proposal Milestone 2
experiments.question: Does the corrected adapter reach the proposal's Milestone 2 target of >=15% relative DS-WER improvement over Gladia?
experiments.conclusion: On the 39 frozen validation windows (31 meetings, 250 reference term occurrences) DS-WER is: Soniox 0.3280, Scribe v2 0.3720, ours (artifact-ct2-fixed) 0.4880, base whisper 0.5400, Gladia 0.5880. Relative improvement over Gladia +17.0%, so the >=15% target is MET on the point estimate that the plan defined it on - but the 95% meeting-block interval on the absolute delta is [-0.1869, +0.0040] and includes zero. Excluding the two roll-call windows our DS-WER (0.4751) is indistinguishable from base whisper's (0.4696). Our error profile on names is 90 substitutions to 28 deletions.
experiments.decision: Report Milestone 2 as met on the preregistered point-estimate definition and never without the interval. The standing finding is not the milestone: on domain terms we make ~50% more errors than Soniox in relative terms, and they are substitutions rather than deletions, which prices exp-2026-07-25-hotwords as the highest-value open direction.
caveats: Retrospectively specified metric: the term lists were written after the 2026-08-11 error analysis existed. The only guard is procedural - lists generated mechanically from OpenCouncil's public city registry, inflections from fixed suffix rules in code, committed before any scoring.

The term lists cover roster surnames and the two city-name terms only. Community names, settlements and local acronyms are excluded because no frozen public source enumerates them, so every DS-WER here is a LOWER BOUND on domain-term error.
The reference is OpenCouncil's own published text: this measures agreement-with-OpenCouncil, not fidelity-to-audio.
The denominator is concentrated: 4 of 39 windows carry 134 of the 250 term occurrences. Leave-one-window-out moves the delta vs Gladia from -0.100 to -0.069 (31%) without reversing its sign.
The base-whisper arm ran on the HuggingFace serverless pipeline, a different decoder stack. Its comparison is not a clean weights comparison.
argos+orestiada is VALIDATION, scored repeatedly and used to stop experiments. One seed, one run - the same run as exp-2026-08-10-benchmark-fixed-adapter.

experiments.title: Decode thresholds against the deletion rate
experiments.question: Does moving one of the faster-whisper decode thresholds the server leaves at default lower our deletion rate without costing WER?
experiments.conclusion: No. Six preregistered arms on the 39 frozen windows collapse into TWO distinct decode behaviours. The no-speech gate fired ZERO times across all 39 windows, so arms B (no_speech_threshold=0.8) and C (None, primary) are byte-identical to the control and could not have changed a token; arm E (log_prob_threshold=None) is identical too, because its fallback trigger fired only twice and both times on segments the compression threshold had already sent to fallback. Arms D (temperature=[0.0], primary) and F (compression_ratio_threshold=None) are identical to each other and differ from the control on 3 of 39 windows: micro-WER +0.00042 [-0.00460,+0.00492], deletion rate +0.00235 [-0.00100,+0.00773], insertion rate +0.00025 [-0.00057,+0.00124]. All three point estimates are WORSE and all three intervals cross zero. No arm passes its gate. Control: WER 0.1589, deletions 0.0600, insertions 0.0201, 715 D to 240 I.
experiments.decision: The served decode configuration stays as it is. The finding that matters is mechanistic, not statistical: our deletions are not produced by segment skipping (the gate never fires) and not by the temperature fallback (removing it increases them). The 'deletions are the cheap half' direction from exp-2026-08-11-wer-levers-research does not survive at the decode-config level. The 7 temporal holdout windows were NOT decoded and remain sealed, because the prereg only releases them to confirm an arm that passed.
caveats: The first decode pass was discarded unscored: the plan's (arm, window) seed gave each arm a different random sequence, so arm B differed from the control on the 4 windows that reached a sampling temperature despite being mechanically inert. Re-run with a window-only seed (common random numbers).
Arm D's insertion-rate delta is dominated by one window: removing win_argos_dec5_2025_996850 reverses its sign. The whole D/F result rests on the 3 windows where fallback reached temperature > 0.
CPU int8, 16 threads - not the CUDA pod that produced the benchmark row. Comparisons hold within the experiment only.
beam_size=5 (the code default) throughout; the mini-PC deployment serves with OC_ASR_BEAM=2. Beam was held fixed and not examined, so no arm's result transfers to a beam-2 deployment unchecked.
word_timestamps=False while the server passes True. Held identical across arms.

39 validation windows (argos+orestiada), repeatedly scored; reference is OpenCouncil's published text. Scored with the project's frozen normalizer, not the benchmark's server-side wer-nofillers implementation.

experiments.title: Training on the human-corrected rows only
experiments.question: Under the fixed two-epoch recipe, what does dropping all no_edit rows from the training set do?
experiments.conclusion: Nothing worth having, and the result is SUGGESTIVE only. On the 39 frozen windows the correction-only adapter scores micro-WER 0.1604 against the control's 0.1589: +0.00151 [-0.00761, +0.01018], deletions +0.00378 [-0.00376, +0.01212], insertions +0.00101 [-0.00232, +0.00435]. Every sign is worse, every interval crosses zero, per-window head-to-head is 18 better / 1 tie / 20 worse, and removing one window reverses the sign of the WER delta. The measured difference (0.15 points) is fourteen times smaller than the 2.1-point per-seed spread already known from exp-2026-08-08-mixture-ratio. One interesting pattern, itself inside the noise: substitutions fall (938 -> 899) while deletions rise (715 -> 760).
experiments.decision: Do not rebuild the training set by dropping no_edit rows - it is not the cheap win it looked like. Answering the actual label-provenance question needs a design that holds hours and optimizer steps constant and runs three seeds per arm; below that the noise swallows the signal, as it did here.
caveats: SUGGESTIVE, not decisive, in either direction: one seed per arm against a measured 2.1-point per-seed spread. Preregistered as such before any number existed.

Dropping no_edit changed label provenance, dataset size (22.5h -> 11.2h), optimizer steps (7,242 -> 3,484), example difficulty and speaker/city mix at once. It measures the effect of dropping those rows under a fixed two-epoch recipe; it is NOT a fixed-compute control and does not isolate 'do unverified labels hurt'.

The in-training eval numbers (val_corr 47.17 -> 30.00, val_reg 15.31 -> 5.71) are NOT the result. val_reg's labels are the old pipeline's unverified output, so gains there measure imitation of the old system - the very thing under suspicion.
CPU int8, one machine for both arms. The control arm is eval-A.json from exp-2026-08-12-decode-ablation: same machine, environment, config, seeds and day.
39 validation windows, reference is OpenCouncil's published text: agreement-with-OpenCouncil, not fidelity-to-audio.
Pod ul4z0drp5owiac, A40, ~6h, ~$2.70. Terminated and verified dead; the armed hard deadline was never reached.

experiments.title: Final report: does domain fine-tuning of whisper-large-v3 pay for Greek council transcription?
experiments.question: Taking every measurement in this ledger together, does the corrected adapter improve Greek council transcription enough to matter, and what remains open?
experiments.conclusion: Yes, but modestly and not where it was hoped. artifact-adapter-fixed ties Scribe v2 and Soniox on unseen cities, beats base whisper by 1.87 points and its broken predecessor by 1.58. Three independent cheap levers were tested this cycle and none paid: decode thresholds (the no-speech gate never fires; removing the temperature fallback is worse), label purity (dropping all no_edit rows gives +0.0015 WER, inside noise fourteen times larger), and data scale (prior research: ~1300h for ~0.5 points). What remains points one way and two independent measurements agree on it: names, wrong by one or two characters - 21.6% of error tokens, and a 90-substitution to 28-deletion profile on domain terms. That is a decode-time name lexicon, not more training.
experiments.decision: Ship the corrected adapter to HuggingFace (a decision, not a task - the public weights are still the broken ones and cost 1.58-1.77 points). Spend the remaining effort on exp-2026-07-25-hotwords / the name-lexicon arm of exp-2026-08-11-name-repair. Do not rerun decode-threshold work, correction-only filtering, or data-scale arguments - all three are closed.
caveats: Every headline number rests on argos+orestiada, which is VALIDATION and has been scored repeatedly and used to stop experiments. Treat as optimistically biased.

All benchmark references are OpenCouncil's published text: agreement-with-OpenCouncil, not fidelity-to-audio. The one time fidelity-to-audio was measured the ranking flipped (exp-2026-08-04-ranking-flips), and artifact-adapter-fixed still has no fidelity-to-audio number.
One seed throughout, against a measured 2.1-point per-seed spread - larger than most effects reported.

Cross-stack comparisons: base whisper on HuggingFace serverless, broken adapter on RTX 3090, corrected on A4000, workstreams 1-3 on CPU int8. CPU int8 and CUDA int8 give different tokens from the same artifact.
Workstreams 1-3 are scored with the project's frozen normalizer, not the benchmark's server-side wer-nofillers implementation.
The dataset remains on DPO legal hold (2026-07-17): not publishable. Text-level PII removal does not anonymise it because each row links audio carrying the voice.

experiments.title: Serving-stack ladder: shifted-window consensus decode and N-best rescoring
experiments.question: Can decode-time interventions (insertion-only shifted-window merge; constrained N-best rescoring) plus the name arms compose into a stack that beats Scribe v2 on the benchmark, with each step's delta measured?
experiments.conclusion: One survivor out of four arms. E (post-hoc roster name repair): -0.00252 WER on the 39 validation windows [-0.00437,-0.00107], and on the ONE frozen benchmark look (E applied to the saved 260-window hypotheses of oc-runpod-fixed-2026-08-10, paired, local frozen scorer) -0.00077 pooled [-0.00124,-0.00033], -0.00279 on unseen cities - reproducing the validation number. B hotwords: rejected (+0.34 WER via +133 deletions, CI excludes zero, despite name recall 51->65%). C shifted-window decode: no-go, never built - 91.3% of deletions sit inside decoder-covered spans. D N-best selector: oracle ceiling 0.0071 exists but the preregistered KenLM selector recovered 0% (all 31 LOMO folds chose lambda=0 outright). STANDING FINDING, three independent measurements: the deletions are a property of the adapter weights - thresholds never fire, the audio is covered, and the missing words are absent from all 8 beam hypotheses (22/741 = 3% present). No serving-time technique reaches them. Holdout (opened once): control 0.1147, E fired zero times (no rosters for June-2026 meetings) - E's value is gated on roster availability.
experiments.decision: Deploy E (engineering task, gated by the Βήμα-3 shadow gates of exp-2026-08-11-name-repair, which stays OPEN for deployment + the v2 orthography-conflict aliases). Do not pursue B, C, or D further. Do not claim a Scribe win: E covers ~0.08 of the ~0.74-point pooled gap; the rest is weight-level deletions, reachable only by targeted retraining (deletion/coverage hard examples), which is a product decision, not a serving change. The planned 2-run GPU benchmark ladder was replaced by the paired text-transform look on the existing bench row - cleaner comparison, zero GPU cost.
caveats: Development only on the 39 validation windows; 4-5 arms on the same set carries winner's-curse risk - gates frozen before numbers, benchmark is the single confirmatory stage.

experiments.title: HParl audio-vs-text faithfulness probe and Soniox alignment filter
experiments.question: Are the HParl transcripts faithful to their own audio, and can a Soniox-alignment filter carve a usable training subset out of them?
experiments.conclusion: Usable audio, unusable targets. On 100 random utterances (16 speakers, shards test-00000 seed 20260814 n=40 and train-00023 seed 7 n=60) verified against Soniox: rows without a [UNK] placeholder disagree at 6.1% WER with a 1.9% deletion rate and a 53% exact-match rate - i.e. the feared editorial-rewrite defect is NOT present at segment level. What disqualifies the corpus is target format: 52-60% of rows in each of three shards read carry at least one [UNK] placeholder over real speech (drives the pooled 7.7% deletion rate), and ZERO rows in any shard carry an accent or punctuation mark - the references are lowercase, unaccented, unpunctuated, while our labels are accented, punctuated clean-verbatim. Segments are ~3s-boundary alignment windows (median 4.7s / 9 tokens), so words are chopped at the edges. Storage is not a constraint: 32 kbps mono MP3 is 4.1 kB/s, ~1.8 GB for the full ~120h. ADDENDUM same day: the ML-processed mirror Elormiden/Hellenic-greek-parliamentary-speech (92,133 clips, 13.8 GB) is the usable one - 99.9% of rows are ACCENTED and none carry [UNK], but 59% carry <spoken_noise> markers and 0% carry punctuation. Filter run (eval/hparl2_filter.py, 150 random rows of test-00000, seed 20260814, tags stripped, alignment = 1 - WER on greek_normalize tokens): pooled WER 0.093 (sub .047 / del .028 / ins .018); align>=0.95 keeps 49% of rows = 50% of audio (~60h of 120h), align>=0.90 keeps 59%, align>=0.80 keeps 81%. TWO CAVEATS ON THAT 60h: (a) median row is 9 reference tokens so >=0.95 is effectively an exact-match test - it selects easy audio and yields a Soniox-agreement sample, not a random one; (b) <spoken_noise> is NOT the discriminator, keep rate is 48% on tagged vs 52% on untagged rows. The lowercase/unpunctuated target problem survives the filter untouched. ddamianos/hparl local cache deleted 2026-08-14. PUNCTUATION STAGE 2026-08-14: eval/hparl2_punctuate.py builds the label as dataset-words + Soniox-punctuation. Deterministic transfer() marks 96% of the 74 kept rows but copies Soniox's terminal period onto fragments (64/74 end in a final mark). gpt-5.6-luna (via the codex bridge, batches of 25, low effort) was run under a HARD WORD GUARD - output is accepted only if its greek_normalize token sequence is identical to the dataset transcript: 74/74 passed, zero words changed. It differs from transfer() on 61/74 rows, and judges only 19/74 (26%) of segments to be COMPLETE SENTENCES, with terminal punctuation matching that judgement 19/19. Three quarters of this corpus's segments are fragments; a naive punctuation pass would teach a sentence end every ~5s. PILOT PASS LANDED 2026-08-14: 10,133 rows across all 28 shards. keep@0.95 = 46.3% (vs 49% on the 150-row sample), pooled WER 0.100 (sub .052 / del .030 / ins .017), 6.18h kept of 13.57h processed, per-shard keep rate 42-52% (median 46%) - extrapolates to ~55h of the 120h. CORRECTION: the earlier claim that <spoken_noise> is NOT a discriminator was an n=150 artifact. At n=10,133 tagged rows keep 40.8% vs untagged 54.1%. The tag is real signal (it marks audio the transcript does not spell out, and the ASR hears it), but it is not sufficient - 41% of tagged rows pass - so admission stays with the alignment score. HUMAN CALIBRATION LANDED 2026-08-14 (43 judged rows, exported from the review page, fetched from the laptop; the two review rounds separated by regenerating both page item lists from their seeds - 29 gate judgements, 13 punctuation judgements, 1 ambiguous and excluded). THE 0.95 GATE IS TOO STRICT: precision is perfect (6/6 kept rows accepted) but 57% of the rows it DROPPED were judged good. By band: align 1.00 100% good (n=6), 0.85-0.95 88% (n=8), 0.50-0.85 75% (n=8), <0.50 0% (n=7) - the cliff is at ~0.50, not 0.95. On the pilot that costs hours: 0.95 keeps 46% of rows / 6.18h, 0.90 keeps 61% / 8.81h, 0.85 keeps 72% / 10.50h (extrapolating 55h vs 78h vs 93h of the 120h). NOT ADOPTED: 6-8 rows per band is a signal, not a calibration, and the page shows the alignment score so the judgement was not blind. Punctuation round: 11/13 accepted (85%), both rejections at align 1.00 i.e. punctuation complaints not row-quality ones. PACK REBUILT 2026-08-14: 4,546 rows / 6.12 h, sha256(train.jsonl)=275516c4fd269af0, 26.2% complete sentences, 145 rows dropped for <3 tokens. Punctuation pass over all 4,693 kept rows: 4,663 LLM outputs accepted, 30 (0.6%) word-guard rejected and fell back to deterministic transfer; the LLM differs from transfer on 88% of rows. BLIND CALIBRATION LANDED 2026-08-14, 62/62 judged, and it overturns the gate. Good control (>0.99) passes 6/6 yes. Band 0.80-0.95: 25/25 yes. Band 0.50-0.80: 22 yes / 3 idk / 0 no. BAD CONTROL (<0.40) FAILS: 3 yes / 1 idk / 2 no - half the rows scored below 0.40 do say their text. They are 1-2s clips where Soniox returned something unrelated, so a low alignment score mostly means SONIOX FAILED, not that the label is wrong: the gate has been measuring ASR confidence and charging the corpus for it. Against the 62 judgements: align>=0.95 admits 6 and throws away 50 good rows; >=0.85 admits 26, throws away 30; >=0.50 admits 56 with ZERO bad rows and throws away 3; >=0.50 + dur>=1.5s admits 53 (51 yes / 2 idk / 0 no) and throws away 5. Both 'no' rows are align 0.00 AND under 1.5s, so a duration floor removes the failure mode. The 4 'don't know' rows are boundary clipping ('the start was cut, I heard half the first word') and ALL FOUR carry a missing first/last reference token - but those flags also fire on 28 human-approved rows, so edge flags are a DOWN-WEIGHTING signal, not an admission rule. Pilot yield: >=0.50 + dur>=1.5s keeps 93% of rows / 13.22h of 13.57h, extrapolating ~117h of the 120h vs 55h at the current gate. hparl2-v2 BUILT 2026-08-14 at the preregistered gate: 9,334 rows / 13.16 h (11.66 h weighted), sha256=29f4fe806b88e80a, 24.2% edge-clipped at weight 0.5, 22.8% complete sentences; 439 rows dropped under 1.5s, 102 under 3 tokens. 2.2x the hours of v1 from the same pilot audio.
experiments.decision: Do not stage HParl as-is. Two routes if it is ever revisited: (a) audio-only with pseudo-labels, which is vendor distillation and inherits the vendor's deletions - not recommended while exp-2026-08-13-targeted-deletion-training is trying to remove exactly that failure mode; (b) keep only [UNK]-free rows (~45%, ~54h) and restore accents+punctuation, accepting that the restoration model then sets the label standard. Ranking from 2026-08-11 stands: the 199 in-domain hours precede this. Licence still unverified at source (HF mirror cc-by-4.0 vs CLARIN 1602 reported CC BY-NC 4.0). 2026-08-14: filter + local review page built (eval/hparl2_filter.py, scripts/hparl2_review_page.py); user audit of a stratified 38-row sample pending before any keep-rate is trusted.

EuroSpeech greece keep=23% (WER .285) BUT the boundary-edge flags explain it: edge-flagged rows (33% of the sample) keep 0% at WER .627 / del .275, while clean-edge rows keep 35% at WER .102 and del .019 - the same 1.9% deletion rate measured on HParl's placeholder-free rows. EuroSpeech's minutes are as faithful as HParl's; the headline was alignment slop, mostly at the END (last ref token missing on 26% of rows, first on 7%). The Codex-suggested edge flags are load-bearing, not decoration. ds_wer preselect calibration is monotone (keep 100/43/35/13% for ds_wer <.05/.05-.10/.10-.20/>=.20) so it can prioritise Soniox spend but must never admit a row; top two bins have n=10 total, so no threshold may be fitted yet. GATE CORRECTION 2026-08-14: the align>=0.95 rule these keep rates were measured against was overturned by the hparl2 blind calibration (it mostly measures whether Soniox succeeded on a 1-2s clip). Rescored against the preregistered replacement (align>=0.50 AND dur>=1.5s, edges down-weighted not rejected): STOMA 70%->100%, CV 65%->99%, EuroSpeech 23%->85%; dropping clipped-edge rows instead costs 100->88%, 99->85%, 85->66%. EuroSpeech was the most distorted, as its boundary analysis predicted. These are rescorings of the existing pilots, not new runs, and no human has judged a STOMA/CV/EuroSpeech clip - the calibration was done on hparl2 and is carried across on the argument that the failure mode belongs to the verifier, not the corpus. LICENCE CORRECTION 2026-08-14 (user-raised, verified on the HF card): EuroSpeech is NOT blocked the way HParl is. HParl's restriction is the CLARIN/ILSP PACKAGING (compilation offered CC BY-NC); EuroSpeech claims no licence of its own and cites, for Greece, n.2121/1993 art. 2(5) (official State texts fall outside copyright) plus art. 25(1)(b) - a statutory exception on the underlying proceedings, so there is no NC term to clear and commercial use is open. The earlier framing 'needs the same legal call as HParl' was wrong. Narrower items still for a lawyer: whether the cited articles cover the AUDIO and not only transcripts, and whether the disco-eth compilation imposes anything itself (its card disclaims responsibility for the licence table's accuracy). CONSEQUENCE: Greek parliamentary speech was never the blocked resource - one compilation's terms were. EuroSpeech offers the same domain at 20x the hours with commercial use open, so it should supersede hparl2 as the parliament source rather than sit behind it.

experiments.title: Minimum detectable effect and coverage of the 39-window evaluation harness
experiments.question: What is the smallest effect the frozen 39-window harness can actually see, is it vulnerable to single-item domination, and can coverage be widened cheaply without touching the freeze?
experiments.conclusion: MDE is not one number - it depends on the arm's shape. Measured 95% CI half-widths give MDE at 80% power: 0.24 for a surgical post-hoc arm (arm E), 0.69 for a decode ablation, 1.27 for a different adapter under the same decode, 1.37 for hotword biasing, 2.66 for us-vs-commercial, and ~2.94 single-seed (SD 1.05) rising to ~3.2 in composition. Arm E's -0.25 sits EXACTLY on its own threshold, not comfortably above it. WER is NOT vulnerable to single-item domination (18/39 windows for 50% of tokens, 12/39 for 50% of errors, LOO <=0.94 points). DS-WER v2 entities already separates 0.488 from 0.328 (+0.175 [0.093,0.258], MDE80 ~0.117) though its top 4 windows carry 51.5% of N. A 63-window extension exists at ZERO human cost (60 training-unseen meetings, 7 cities, 18,821 tokens, human references already in the public benchmark, outside the freeze and outside holdout, ~103 CPU-minutes per arm) but buys only 15% narrower CIs and is POORER in entities (8.9 vs 21.0 per 1,000 tokens). The blind spot is seeds, not windows, and more windows do not fix it.
experiments.decision: Do not treat excludes_zero as a sufficient gate for single-sign post-hoc arms: with 31 blocks the paired bootstrap excludes zero for ANY single-sign arm touching >=4 meetings regardless of effect size ((1-4/31)^31 = 0.014 < 0.025). Arm E touches 11, so its excludes_zero was guaranteed by construction - this does not invalidate arm E (the benchmark look supplies the magnitude independently) but it does retire the gate. Replacement gate is an open decision.
caveats: MDE figures are derived from ALREADY MEASURED CI half-widths on this freeze, not from a prospective power analysis; they describe what this harness has done, and assume a new arm resembles one of the listed shapes.

experiments.title: 2026 landscape scan: what attacks deletions and names in low-resource ASR
experiments.question: What techniques available in 2026 attack our two specific errors - silent speech omissions and surname/toponym substitutions - rather than general WER, and which fit the remaining GSoC runway?
experiments.conclusion: Ranked for the remaining runway: (1) cross-system ROVER fusion with Soniox and Scribe - the only item that BYPASSES 'the deletions live in the weights', since words absent from all our beams are present in their transcripts; 0 GPU, ~4-8 human-hours. (2) Roster-grounded constrained correction, RECOVER-style phonetic retrieval plus a Krikri-8B editor, working over a CLOSED list; literature reports 8-46% relative E-WER without overall WER regression. (3) NeMo canary-1b-v2 with GPU-PB/TurboBias ACOUSTIC-level word boosting (not prompt-level) - the mechanism that explains why our hotword arm paid +133 deletions; FLEURS el 9.21 verified on the model card, zero-shot measurement only within 5 days. Four assumption-breaking findings: VoxKrikri (ILSP, arXiv:2509.15667) is trained ON HParl and beats whisper-large-v3 13.01 vs 16.99 in the same table, so the corpus we deprioritised as 'unusable targets' worked for someone else; NO reference-free detector for missing speech spans exists in 2026 (the entire hallucination-detection literature targets EXTRA text, and Whisper-CD's numbers come from degenerate baselines at WER 208 and 520, which do not transfer to our 0.1377); LLM-based generative error correction is documented to DEGRADE named entities and to worsen baselines in low-error regimes, an independent confirmation of our own arm D failure; and NeMo has no official LoRA recipe for Canary/Parakeet, only full fine-tuning at 20-80 A100-hours per 100h.
experiments.decision: Keep fusion first in the runway - the landscape independently confirms the ordering already chosen. Do not attempt a backbone swap or an LLM rewriter within this cycle. Any LLM in the fusion arm must SELECT among candidates, never rewrite.
caveats: Literature scan via grok-research with citations, not reproduction: no number in this report was measured by us, and none has been reproduced on our data.
VoxKrikri carries a licence discrepancy - Apache-2.0 on HuggingFace, Llama 3.1 Community in the paper - which must be resolved before any use.
Published Greek WER figures (FLEURS, Common Voice) are read-speech benchmarks and do not transfer to long-form council audio; they rank candidates, they do not predict our numbers.
This scan does NOT reopen exp-2026-08-14-hparl-probe: the CLARIN 1602 licence question that put it out of scope is untouched by it.

experiments.title: pyannoteAI precision-2 with transcription: fourth voter, omission detector, word-level speaker
experiments.question: Does pyannoteAI precision-2 with transcription:true and exclusive:true give a useful fourth ASR voter, a lower deletion rate by virtue of a monotonic transducer, and a reference-free detector for missing speech?
experiments.conclusion: One of three. (1) Parakeet-TDT-0.6b-v3 is NOT usable for Greek council audio: WER 0.3567 against the corrected adapter's 0.1386, zero wins in 247 windows (+0.2181), and 78% of its error is substitutions - it does not lose speech, it does not know Greek. Published FLEURS/Common Voice figures do not transfer, as preregistered. (2) As a fourth voter it adds nothing: -0.0014 WER and -0.0009 del_rate, both CIs include zero, and the four-way oracle is IDENTICAL to the three-way oracle to four decimals - it is the best system in no window at all. THE MONOTONICITY HYPOTHESIS IS DISPROVEN: its deletion rate is 0.0453, 3.2x Soniox's 0.0142 and statistically indistinguishable from our own autoregressive adapter's 0.0459. Being a transducer did not buy a lower deletion rate. (3) The omission detector WORKS: intervals where exclusiveDiarization asserts speech while our transcript has no words hit real deletions at precision 0.320 against a fair random-interval null of 0.094 (+0.226 [+0.144,+0.324], CI excludes zero), recall 0.101. A precision alarm, not a net - and it is the only publishable piece here, since no reference-free detector for missing speech spans exists in the 2026 literature. Cost $1.88-$3.13 for 250 jobs / 10.16 audio hours, zero failures, zero GPU. | ROUND 2 (faster-whisper-large-v3-turbo as the STT, same 247 windows, $1.88-3.13, billing confirmed per audio-hour not compute-time): Whisper-turbo alone WER 0.1666 / del 0.0423 - usable Greek, unlike Parakeet's 0.3567, but not competitive: worse than plain large-v3 (+0.0207) and than our adapter (+0.0281), both CIs exclude zero. As a FOURTH VOTER IT WON, against the agent's own preregistered null: -0.00448 WER [-0.00799,-0.00160], CI excludes zero - but the gain is in INSERTIONS (0.0443 -> 0.0385), not deletions (-0.00004, CI includes zero), and the voter is correlated with our backbone by construction. THE SPEAKER-INFORMATION QUESTION, which was the user's actual goal: NO overall, YES inside overlap. Per-turn selection beats per-window (-0.0036, CI excludes zero) but a PLACEBO of equally many cuts at non-speaker boundaries beats it MORE (-0.0056); turn minus placebo = +0.0020 [+0.0004,+0.0037], i.e. speaker cuts are WORSE - what wins is locality, not speaker identity. Without that control the finding would have been reported as 'speaker information helps by 0.36 points' and would have been false. Restricted to the 823 cells with DETECTED OVERLAP (24,079 tokens) the sign REVERSES: turn minus placebo = -0.00558 [-0.00888,-0.00228], CI excludes zero, 166 wins / 56 ties / 96 losses. Using the transcript to separate speakers works, and only where they talk over each other. OMISSION DETECTOR, prediction DISPROVEN: the regular diarization finds LESS missing speech than exclusive (108 flags, R=0.107 vs 125, R=0.134), for a structural reason - in an interval {A,B} a single word from A blocks the flag even if all of B's turn was lost, so a 'no words of ours here' rule cannot see the loss of one speaker inside simultaneous speech. A per-speaker density rule is needed and was deliberately NOT tried, since it would be threshold selection after the numbers. ERROR LOCALISATION, the most directly actionable result: 5.1% of tokens near a speaker handover carry 11.4% of reference-side errors, and the 2.45% inside overlap carry 7.3% (del 0.0599 vs 0.0238, +0.0361 [+0.0193,+0.0535]) - identifiable today without a reference, and a targeting signal for exp-2026-08-13-targeted-deletion-training.
experiments.decision: Do not add Parakeet as a voter and do not pursue faster-whisper-turbo through this API as an ASR source. Keep exclusiveDiarization as an omission-detection signal: it is the one place where an acoustic model supplies evidence our own hypotheses cannot. The CTC/transducer-monotonicity argument for a Whisper CTC head is weakened by this result and must not be quoted as motivation without acknowledging it. ROUND 2: do not adopt Whisper-turbo as a production voter - it is correlated with our backbone and its win is in insertions only. DO pursue speaker-aware selection INSIDE detected overlap, where it is measured to work. Any future claim that 'speaker information helps selection' must carry the placebo control, which reversed the naive reading.
caveats: SEAL BREACH FOUND AND CONTAINED: 6 of the 7 sealed temporal holdout windows of eval-freeze-2026-08 sit inside the 253-window benchmark report. They were excluded here (n=247) and every comparison recomputed on the same 247. The same breach had already affected exp-2026-08-16-fusion-deletions, which was corrected in the same change.

ROUND 2's fourth-voter win contradicts the agent's own preregistered expectation of a null. It is reported as measured, with the constraint that the gain is insertion-side only and the voter is not independent of our backbone.

The omission detector's per-speaker density rule was NOT tried on purpose: choosing that threshold after seeing the numbers would be selection on the result. It is the obvious next step and is unmeasured.

Two Codex reviews ran before any number was seen. The first introduced the placebo control that reversed the headline. The second found a speaker-scan bug (set of labels instead of counts) and a handover definition that MISSED handovers via overlap ({A}->{A,B}->{B}) - precisely the transitions the experiment was about. Locked with 15 tests.

The omission detector's ground truth is agreement-with-OpenCouncil, not a human listening to the audio, so precision 0.320 is a LOWER BOUND: a span our reference also omits counts as a false positive here.

Two measurement errors were caught by Codex review (high effort) BEFORE any number was seen: the random null was unfair (random intervals could land in silence) and the time interpolation snapped extreme deletion runs onto adjacent recognised speech. Both fixed and declared on the issue before analysis.

experiments.title: Glossary provenance, leakage extent, and distillation to a usable term list
experiments.question: Can the 2026-06-20 glossary's provenance be proven, how far does its leakage reach into the benchmark, and which of its terms deserve a place beside the frozen roster and per-city lists?
experiments.conclusion: Provenance PROVEN: scripts/glossary_manifest.py re-runs the miner over the reconstructed TRAIN fold and reproduces glossary.json BYTE-IDENTICAL (sha256 f5101f6c...), from 317 (city, meeting) pairs across 22 cities. THE LEAKAGE IS WORSE THAN THE TICKET ASSUMED: the glossary's fold is the eval harness hash-split, NOT the fine-tune's training manifest, and it covers MORE of the benchmark. Of the 253 common windows, 178 are in the glossary fold, 148 in the fine-tune train, 213 in at least one - only 40 are disjoint from BOTH. So 65 of the 105 windows the ticket called 'training-disjoint' are contaminated for a glossary arm, and bench_data.training_meetings() is the WRONG line to split on. Codex adds that even those 40 are not clean held-out, since the benchmark was already used developmentally when the global list was abandoned - so any glossary arm is exploratory, not confirmatory. DISTILLATION: from 3,543 per-city candidates, 853 passed the filters but only 35 carried category evidence (818 left as 'unverified' and NOT proposed); from 748 acronym candidates, 14 survived cross-city with expansions from gpt-5.6-luna; from 173 institutional/legal proposals, ZERO survived. Final: 47 terms for human review. The 5,894-term global list contributed nothing.
experiments.decision: USER DECISION 2026-08-16: the 'no terms from transcripts' rule is WITHDRAWN as a category error - a correction lexicon is not a training set, and transcripts are the correct source because they carry the terms that actually recur. Admission is now governed by COLLISION SAFETY, not provenance: a term earns its place if it recurs across meetings and cannot be confused with ordinary language. That test already exists and already works (it cut AMEA, a genuine term, at 88.9 similarity against the everyday word 'amesa'; AMEA stays out). The split survives FOR MEASUREMENT ONLY: any arm using these lists reports on windows disjoint from the mining fold (40 of 253 here), because that is the number that predicts an unmined city. Recorded in docs/decisions/data.md. The 47 candidates are admissible on provenance grounds; per-term human review is still outstanding.
caveats: The 'missing legal/administrative term list' was NOT missing: 52 `procedural` terms already exist in build_ds_wer_terms_v2.py, built in August from the same Standard Regulation (FEK B' 109/2025). Of 173 terms gpt-5.6-luna proposed after reading 24 whole meetings, 29 were already there and the rest fell as everyday language or as non-recurring. The real gap was ACRONYMS, not phrases.

AMEA was cut despite being a genuine term: it scores 88.9 similarity against the ordinary word 'amesa' under the production scorer, so admitting it risks corrupting correct text. This is the precision principle working as intended.

Four bugs were found AFTER numbers were seen and are declared in the report; the most serious is that el_GR.dic is iso-8859-7, so the common-word check was silently loading 25 entries instead of 828,000.
35 of the 47 candidates carry category evidence; the remaining 818 per-city candidates sit in an 'unverified' tier and are deliberately NOT proposed.
No terms/*.json file was modified. The distillation output is a candidate list awaiting human review, not an admitted list.

experiments.title: Mining correction terms from the error database rather than the transcripts
experiments.question: The #19 distillation returned 47 terms, all acronyms and zero toponyms. Does mining the human-correction database instead of raw transcripts recover the toponyms and person names, and which terms deserve admission?
experiments.conclusion: YES, and the composition changes completely: 147 survivors from 667 mined keys - 68 toponyms, 33 person names, 33 acronyms, 13 organisations - against #19's 47 all-acronym set. No threshold was relaxed; the collision filters are imported from glossary_distill.py unchanged. What changed is the witness: data/asr/export.jsonl puts the model's wrong form next to the human's right answer, which proves category in a way a transcript cannot, plus OSM gazetteers (settlements, STREETS, named public buildings) for all 11 cities rather than just argos/orestiada. Ranking is by how many times a human corrected the term, not by frequency. Tiers: injection 0, metric-only 9, review 83, review-backlog 55. THE HEADLINE IS NOT THE YIELD: the single highest-benefit candidate in the entire mining run, SCHOINA (corrected 11 times in Chania), IS ALREADY IN THAT CITY'S FROZEN LIST - as are VRILISSION (6), DEDDIE (5), KANELLOPOULOU (5) and MAXIADIZ (4). 26 terms fell to C0 (already present) while carrying >=2 human corrections each. The top of the benefit distribution is not terms we lack; it is terms we HAVE and the model keeps breaking. The binding constraint is application, not discovery.
experiments.decision: The 147 candidates are a REVIEW QUEUE, not an admitted list; no terms/*.json file was modified. The injection tier is deliberately empty: a post-hoc zipf==0 exemption when a gazetteer corroborates the term would have promoted 3, and Codex rejected it as post hoc, so it survives only as a labelled sensitivity count. Open #19 items resolved: NEGRI is the second element of the street name 'Fokionos Negri' (now an implementation rule, not a term); MAXIADIZ is the registered name of a Zografou municipal company, genuine, corrected 4x; LOATKI is linguistically universal but attested only in Athens in every pool, so it is NOT promoted cross-city - the earlier reading that it is cross-city was not supported by the data.
experiments.next_action: The finding redirects the work: before adding any of these 147 terms, establish why the terms already in the frozen lists do not survive - SCHOINA is present and was still corrected 11 times by hand. That is a question about the repair/selection point (point A), not about lexicon coverage. Any arm using these lists reports on windows disjoint from the mining fold and is exploratory, not confirmatory (see exp-2026-08-16-glossary-distillation).
caveats: Clean windows for any downstream measurement: 31/39 validation. The 7 sealed holdout windows were left sealed and were NOT scored.
